learn.title: Parts of a whole
learn.body: A fraction names equal parts of a whole. In $\frac{3}{4}$ the denominator (4) says the whole is cut into 4 equal parts, and the numerator (3) says we take 3 of them. A fraction is also a division: $\frac{3}{4}=3\div 4$.

learn.title: Equivalent fractions
learn.body: Different fractions can name the same amount. Multiply the top and bottom by the same number and the value does not change: $\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3\times 2}{4\times 2}=\frac{6}{8}$. Both fractions cover the same part of the whole.

learn.title: Simplifying
learn.body: To simplify, divide the top and bottom by a common factor. A fraction is in simplest form when the GCF of the top and bottom is 1. Remember the GCF from the last unit: it gives the fastest route.

learn.title: Simplify $\frac{18}{24}$
learn.body: Find the GCF of 18 and 24, then divide both by it.
steps: Divide the top and bottom by 6: $\frac{18\div 6}{24\div 6}$.

learn.title: Improper fractions and mixed numbers
learn.body: If the top is bigger than the bottom, the fraction is more than 1. $\frac{7}{3}$ means 7 thirds. Three thirds make 1 whole, so it is 2 wholes and 1 third left: $2\frac{1}{3}$. A number like that is a mixed number.
To compare fractions, give them the same denominator. $\frac{4}{5}=\frac{16}{20}$ and $\frac{3}{4}=\frac{15}{20}$, so $\frac{4}{5}$ is greater.

questions.explanation: Multiply top and bottom by 3: $\frac{9}{12}$. The others have a different value.
Divide both parts by 2 to get $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.prompt: Which is the simplest form of $\frac{18}{24}$?
questions.explanation: Both other choices still have a common factor of 2 or 3. The GCF is 6, which gives $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.prompt: Match each improper fraction with its mixed number.
questions.explanation: Divide the top by the bottom. The quotient is the whole part and the remainder is the new top.

questions.prompt: Simplify $\frac{12}{18}$. Put the steps in order.
steps: Find the GCF of 12 and 18, which is 6
Divide the top and bottom by 6
questions.explanation: Dividing both parts by the GCF gives the simplest form in one step.
